Cause: The search-api pods (image tag 4.8.0) now run two containers — `api` (cpu request 1) and a new `log-forwarder` sidecar (fluent/fluent-bit:3.1.4) that has no resources set. The HPA uses a Resource/cpu Utilization target, and when any container in the pod is missing the relevant resource request, pod CPU utilization is undefined and the HPA takes no action — which is exactly the `cpu <unknown>/60%` symptom and why it has been pinned at the 3-replica minimum since 4.8.0 [cite: concepts/workloads/autoscaling/horizontal-pod-autoscale#how-does-a-horizontalpodautoscaler-work-3].

Evidence: `kubectl get pods -n catalog` shows all 3 search-api pods have containers [api, log-forwarder]; log-forwarder has `resources: {}` (no cpu/memory request). Before 4.8.0 there was only one container, so utilization was always defined.

Fix (choose one, owner can apply):
1) Add a cpu request to the log-forwarder sidecar in the Deployment pod spec (e.g. `resources.requests.cpu: 50m`). Resource-metric HPAs compute utilization as a percentage of the container's cpu request, so every container needs one [cite: concepts/workloads/autoscaling/horizontal-pod-autoscale#support-for-resource-metrics-0].
2) Or switch the HPA metric from `type: Resource` to `type: ContainerResource` targeting only the `api` container, which lets the HPA ignore the sidecar's usage [cite: concepts/workloads/autoscaling/horizontal-pod-autoscale#container-resource-metrics-0] [cite: concepts/workloads/autoscaling/horizontal-pod-autoscale#container-resource-metrics-1].

Either change will restore CPU utilization reporting and let the HPA scale search-api up at lunchtime again.
